label: pjm 36 retiree cems
definition: NEW KEEPER (supersedes pjm 35 cc-steam). pjm_35 config + within-window retiree CEMS measured-availability cap (retiree_cems_cap=True): each within-window retiree plant is limited to its measured monthly CAMPD CEMS envelope (zero in months it did not run), honestly reflecting the out-of-market retirement economics a cost-based LP cannot see — nothing tuned to the coal/net-MWh target. Closes the Homer City (3122) phantom-baseload over: model 4.40/2.79/0.00 → 1.48/0.00/0.00 TWh vs CEMS 1.20/0.00/0.00. Two compounding fixes: (a) per-unit COD retirement in cod_ramp (effective_cod no longer collapses heterogeneous unit retirements to the latest date) — MAE-neutral alone, the per-plant binning merges units before the ramp; (b) the CEMS cap, which moves the aggregate. Coal-tot: 2023 +15.7%→+13.8%, 2024 +5.0%→+3.1% (now PASS), 2025 +8.7% unchanged (no running retirees — clean blast radius). In-tolerance fails 7→5; freed retiree energy split between gas (stays PASS) and reduced 2023 over-export (interchg +15.0%→+11.6%). Finding: the residual operable-coal over (2025 +7.8% BIT, confound-free) is system merit-order, NOT a retiree-capacity issue.
